groups.title: Four staves: independent descenders
groups.notes: Four staves occupy columns 1, 3, 5 and 7; column 0 remains blank. The native Unifont m shoulder sequence is compacted to one crest pixel per two-column interval. The initial stave retains its head pixel at (1,6), while internal staves start at row 7 beneath supported diagonal crests. As in native m, joined staves have no additional base serifs. All three underside openings remain open through the baseline; optional middle descenders add only their two designated pixels below it.

groups.title: Long bowl: only the adjacent ascender closes it
groups.notes: The turned arches are drawn on the unchanged Latin body rows, following native turned m and u hips, rather than rotating the entire 16-row cell. The long left bowl occupies columns 1 through 3 from row 3 to row 13. Its one-pixel open return is at (3,5), immediately above the adjacent first middle arm. Extending that arm fills the opening; extending the farther arm at column 5 leaves it open. Compound ascenders use the unadorned vertical terminals of native h and q, avoiding head-serifs that would bridge neighboring staves.

groups.title: Shared spine: independent descender and ascender
groups.notes: The four staves remain at columns 1, 3, 5 and 7. The shared spine crosses at row 9, leaving a two-pixel upper counter and a three-pixel lower counter in column 4. Its left arch enters through the row-6 crest and its right hip exits through (6,13). The upper hook keeps its open return; the lower hook ends in the compact leftward bend used by native eng. Independent extensions preserve the complete shared-spine body.

reviewNotes: The left-only and both states close exactly the same long bowl; the right-only state leaves the opening at (3,5) unchanged.
The first extension overlaps the pre-existing returning terminal at (3,4), so its visible difference adds two pixels, (3,3) and (3,5).
The extended right outer stem reaches rows 3 and 15 without gaining a broad dotless-i foot.

glyphs.notes: Use the approved four-stave body at columns 1, 3, 5, 7 with its row-9 crossover and two open central counters of two and three pixels. The left shoulder enters below its crest; the right hip leaves above the baseline. Joined staves retain simple native n/m/u endings. Middle components follow allocation order from left to right; only their designated upper or lower extension pixels change between states. Outer curved terminals use the native-f crest and contextual native-y or script-g return; no extra tip, serif, or enclosed terminal pocket is added. This allocation contains no declared long bowl or returnContact, so ordinary compact hooks are not forced to close against unrelated staves. The two-column native-y hip rises to row 12 without altering the central spine; its tipless lower return occupies the single interior pixel at row 15.
reviewNotes: The row-9 crossover separates the upper counter at (4,7..8) from the lower counter at (4,10..12).
The right hip connects through (6,13) to (5,12) and (7,13).
The lower hook ends at (5,15) and (6,15), with (5,14) left blank so its return stays open.
Both hook apertures and all extension differences are unchanged.
